result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain that six overlapping font families cause the messy look, point out the Courier New phone number and the serif-sans-serif switches between heading levels, and suggest a shorter set of fonts. B also handles fallbacks properly, with real system font stacks, a note on what happens when web fonts fail to load, and a warning about browsers faking bold and italic. A only says that loading fewer font files makes pages faster. A's fix keeps the fonts the clinic already uses and is slightly simpler to adopt, but B covers more of the rubric without becoming a tutorial. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers find the core problem: six overlapping families, near-duplicate sans faces, a heading order that jumps serif → sans → serif, and Courier New on the phone number. Both give a concrete two-family replacement and address older readers well. A is ahead because it gives real fallback stacks and points out missing fallbacks and synthesized weights. B only mentions loading fewer font files, though reusing the existing Open Sans is a practical choice.
